prompt:
You run weekly onboarding A/B tests. Here is every finished test so far: what you predicted
and what was measured.

- round 1: Move Sign-In After Pet Adoption [sign_in, reorder]: predicted +12.0%, measured +16.8% (p=0.0), won
- round 1: Interactive Desktop Control Guide on Finish [finish, new_flow]: predicted +10.0%, measured -6.6% (p=0.207102), lost: no clear effect
- round 1: Instant Ready-to-Adopt Pet Choice Grid [adoption, layout]: predicted +15.0%, measured +2.4% (p=0.561281), lost: no clear effect
- round 1: Time Estimate & Error Safeguard on Waiting Screen [home, wait_info]: predicted +8.0%, measured -3.5% (p=0.257077), lost: no clear effect
- round 1: Clear Path Selection Copy [choose_path, copy]: predicted +8.0%, measured +0.6% (p=0.771416), lost: no clear effect
- round 2: Account Sync Safeguard Warning [sign_in, hint]: predicted +3.0%, measured +4.2% (p=0.052352), lost: no clear effect
- round 2: Desktop Tray Status Notification Prompt [finish, notification]: predicted +2.0%, measured -5.4% (p=0.320894), lost: no clear effect
- round 2: Generation Status Live Progress Visualizer [home, wait_info]: predicted +2.0%, measured +9.3% (p=0.002069), won

Previous lessons:
Reordering onboarding steps (moving sign-in after pet adoption) significantly improved performance and exceeded predictions (+16.8% measured vs +12.0% predicted).
New flow guides on finish screens showed no clear effect, and the predicted impact (+10.0%) was too high.
Adoption grid layout changes showed no clear effect, with predictions (+15.0%) being overly optimistic.
Waiting screen time estimates and error safeguards showed no clear effect, over-predicting impact (+8.0%).
Copy adjustments for path selection showed no clear effect, and predictions (+8.0%) were too high.

Rewrite the lessons: at most 6 short rules about which kinds of change worked, which did not, and
where your predictions were too high or too low. Call a kind of change helpful only if a test of that
kind won (was significant); for tests with no clear effect, say no effect was seen, even if the numbers
lean one way. Keep rules that still hold, drop ones the data contradicts. Return JSON {"lessons": ["..."]}

lessons: Reordering onboarding steps (moving sign-in after adoption) was helpful and exceeded predictions (+16.8% measured vs +12.0% predicted).

Live progress visualizers on the waiting screen were helpful and far exceeded predictions (+9.3% measured vs +2.0% predicted), whereas static time estimates and error safeguards on the same screen showed no clear effect.
Finish screen additions (control guides and notification prompts) showed no clear effect, and predictions were set too high.
Adoption grid layout changes showed no clear effect, with predictions (+15.0%) being overly optimistic.
Copy adjustments for path selection showed no clear effect, over-predicting impact (+8.0%).
Account sync safeguard warnings showed no clear effect, with predictions (+3.0%) being too high.
